correctness.rationale: Each cactus spanning tree deletes one edge independently per cycle with reciprocal-conductance probability. Only original degree-one vertices and degree-two cycle vertices may become tree leaves. Thus the generating function factors into degree-at-most-two cycle terms; the discriminant gives exact real-rootedness. Active/inactive cycle runs obey N >= a+2c+3r, proving every unweighted cactus <=6 is real-rooted and <=9 has log-concave leaf coefficients via convolution closure. The explicit C5 and C8 cycles each with two adjacent pendants give sharp failures at 7 and 10. Exact standalone enumeration verified 101 connected cactus types through 7 vertices, with and without nonconstant positive weights; the finite checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: A complete distribution-shape classification is a natural strengthening of known contiguity of achievable leaf counts. The sharp 7- and 10-vertex thresholds identify the first failure of two important probabilistic polynomial properties in a tractable infinite sparse class, while the positive-weight factorization gives a reusable exact law and real-root criterion. These are globally quantified and structurally motivated, not arbitrary finite slices.
